Raw SSE against a throwaway backend at 8cc907d. graph-full 643994B; then ONE real board change through a product action — renaming this session, which the /rename route publishes at 'sessions' scope — arrived as a graph-delta of 1875B carrying exactly 1 unit: 0.29% of the snapshot it patches. Two further patches followed as the board moved on (12137B / 4 units, 27214B / 11 units); every one of the three was smaller than the full, the first chained from the very tag held at subscribe time, and each later patch's  matched its predecessor's  with no break. The min(patch, full) guarantee and the hash chain both hold on the refactored algebra.

Re-measured on 8cc907d in real Chromium over a worktree vite/backend pair, on the sessions panel. Injected one real board change through a product action — renamed this session to a distinct name — and watched for that name to appear in the rendered DOM while logging every /api/graph response. The scenario's strict clause survives the conditional-key change intact, and is now stricter in a way worth noting — a poll landing in that window would no longer be able to deliver the change anyway, since it would answer 304 against the fingerprint of the board the patch had already installed.
